I, Son Lazaro Compound, Rizal Avenue, Sta Cruz, 1003 Manila Dear Secretary Rosell-Ubial: s. 20.12 This has reference to your letter dated 21 March 2017 requesting for this Department's clarification/legal opinion on the functions of the Local Government Unit (LGUs) in regulating and monitoring the practice of Massage Therapy in the country in relation to the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 856 or "Code on Sanitation of the Philippines". In this regard, a reading of Sections 447 & 458 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC) suggest that although the grant of license to practice a profession is within the jurisdiction of another Board or Commission; however, the LGU has the power to regulate and monitor the practice of profession within its territorial jurisdiction. The relevant provisions are quoted hereunder, to wit: SÜction 447. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - (3) Subject to the provisions of Book II of this Code, grant franchises, enact ordinances authorizing the issuance of permits or licenses, or enact ordinances levying taxes, fees and charges upon such conditions and for such purposes intended to promote the general welfare of the inhabitants of the municipality, and pursuant to this legislative authority shall: (D) Regulate any business, occupation, or practice of profession or calling which oes not uire overmnent examination within the m unicipality and the conditions under which the license for said business or practice of profession may be issued or revoked; Section 458. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation.

(3) Subject to the provisions of Book II of this Code. enact ordnances granting franchises and authorizing the issuance of or licenses, upon such conditions and for such purposes intended to promote the general welfare of the inhabitants of the city and pursuant to this legislative authority shall: (ii) Regulate or fix license fees for any business or practice of profession within the city and the conditions under which the license for said business or practice of profession may be revoked and enact ordinances levying taxes thereon; (Emphasis supplied) In the case of Acebedo vs. CA', the Supreme Court (SC) held that an LGU can still regulate the practice of profession in its jurisdiction pursuant to Section 16 of the LGC or the "General Welfare Clause". Under such clause, an LGU exercises police pov,er in matters affecting the health, safety, peace, order, morals, comfort and t:onvenience of the community. Further, SC in one case, held that police power is essentially regulatory in nature and the power to issue licenses or grant business permits, if exercised for a regulatory and not 2 revenue-raising purpose, is within the ambit of this power . In view of the foregoing, the LGUs can regulate and monitor the practice of massage therapy in their respective territorial jurisdiction. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you.
